title: Show me the proof
subtitle: Claude proved 100+ libraries free of whole bug classes, and auditors went inside a lab to test its watchers: trust is turning into evidence
editor_note: Today's idea: after a week of breaches, the answer is shifting from "trust us" to "here is the proof." Anthropic and Theorem used Claude to formally verify security properties in over a hundred open-source libraries, and Theorem now offers it free to maintainers. The lead goes further: METR and Redwood researchers spent three weeks inside OpenAI testing the monitors that watch its agents, and found a gap after context compaction. Your save asks what CTOs should decide now that AI keeps finding bugs. Field notes add Vercel's push to kill static keys, fake errors that steer an AI operator, and a striking task-length claim. Japan desk sets an AI-run attack beside an 11.7-million-account leak. Further out: the first living-culture 人間国宝, a 70 cm dinosaur footprint, Finland's spent-fuel vault, a new virus in humans, and papers Nature turned down.

sections.headline: Claude proved over 100 open-source libraries free of whole classes of bugs
sections.deck: With Theorem, Anthropic's red team turned formal verification from a months-long expert job into weeks of AI work across real codebases. Theorem now offers it free to open-source projects.
sections.why: Proofs scale where audits do not; a dependency you rely on may qualify for free verification.

sections.headline: Auditors inside the lab: METR tested the monitors watching OpenAI's agents
sections.deck: Three weeks on site with real access found a blind spot after context compaction, and a transparency problem with redactions.
sections.why: If you run agents with monitors, check what they never see: compaction, retries and anything outside the log.

sections.headline: Kill static keys, distrust your error logs, and a bold chart

items.headline: Rauch: make OIDC the new TLS and retire static credentials
items.note: Vercel found only 8.4% of 1,000+ SaaS vendors support secure auth; a stolen short-lived key is worth far less.
items.why: Your CI and agents probably hold long-lived keys right now.
